sentences.text: The future of Poundland hangs in the balance after the discount retailer's collapse into administration.

sentences.text: The People's Party of Alberto Núñez Feijóo is narrowly ahead in most opinion polls After eight years of Socialist-led government under Pedro Sánchez, Spain is at a crossroads.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Snap elections are taking place on Sunday 29 November, and voters face a choice of continued left-wing rule or a conservative-led government, with the likely support of far-right Vox.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Sánchez called this vote eight months early after MPs rejected planned changes to Spain's housing laws.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: He was responding to nationwide protests after an 87-year-old woman called Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her rented flat in Madrid and later died.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: But his government lost the support of a centre-right party called Junts from the north-eastern region of Catalonia which sought to protect the rights of property owners.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Housing remains one of the hot-button issues for voters, but they are also focused on the high cost of living, corruption and immigration.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: And the election takes place within weeks of a devastating rail disaster that has shattered confidence in Spain’s high-speed rail network.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Alberto Núñez Feijóo's conservative People's Party is narrowly ahead of the Socialist PSOE in most polls.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: He has spoken of Spain being probably at "the most significant moment in our country for the past 50 years", and he aims to "repair the state, regenerate democracy, reunited the nation and recover Spain's ambition and self-esteem".
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: But it is unlikely he could do anything without the backing of Vox, who are third in the opinion polls.

sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Spain saw its first general strike for 14 years this month over a shortage of housing and high rental costs Spain's property prices and rents have soared by more than 80% from 2015 to 2025, and wages have not kept pace.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Spain has a combination of high demand and scarce supply: the Bank of Spain estimates 700,000 homes are needed to ease the pressure.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: The result is that millions of Spaniards have little chance to buy a house, while they live in fear of eviction if their rent is increased.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: On 11 November, four million Spaniards were galvanised into joining the first general strike since 2012, according to the unions.
sentences.article_title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake

sentences.text: Pedro Sánchez has embraced housing reform as a big campaign issue and left-wing parties have promised rent controls and protection against eviction, while the right is focusing on building more homes, tax breaks for homebuyers and planning deregulation.

sentences.text: Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba's social media posts have previously sparked diplomatic tensions The Democratic Republic of Congo has summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is also the president's son.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: In a series of X posts, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to support a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo.

sentences.text: He insisted that Uganda's military involvement was purely driven by security concerns.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The DR Congo's foreign ministry summoned Uganda's envoy to explain the remarks, describing them as "particularly serious" and damaging to diplomatic relations.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The Ugandan government has yet to respond.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The diplomatic row comes despite close military ties between the neighbours.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: Their forces have been conducting joint operations against the Islamic State-linked Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern DR Congo since 2021.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: Uganda has also recently been involved in efforts to mediate between the Congolese government and an armed group led by former warlord Thomas Lubanga in Ituri province.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The Bahema are a traditionally cattle-herding community mainly based in DR Congo's north-eastern Ituri province.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: They have historical and cultural ties to the Bahima people of neighbouring Uganda.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: He also threatened a rebel takeover of Walikale, in North Kivu province, while defending Uganda's military presence in DR Congo.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: Walikale is rich in mineral resources , including some of the country's largest tin deposits and several major gold mines.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: Gen Kainerugaba's X account, which had nearly 1.4 million followers, has since become inaccessible.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: It is unclear whether he deactivated it, as he has done in the past, or whether the platform had suspended it.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: During the same week he declared: "My tweets in Uganda are directives that must be obeyed." The posts followed reports that a DR Congo military aircraft had allegedly been shot down by rebels , with foreign mercenaries reportedly among those on board.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: Gen Kainerugaba criticised the reported presence of foreign mercenaries in DR Congo.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: "These remarks, which are particularly serious, have caused a major media incident and undermine the necessary restraint that must prevail in relations between sovereign states," the DR Congo foreign ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: "The Congolese government expects the Republic of Uganda to clarify its official position and take the necessary measures to prevent such transgressions from recurring in the future".
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The ministry added that DR Congo remained committed to regional peace and stability but would defend its dignity and institutions against "any form of provocation or interference".
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: In 2024, DR Congo also summoned Uganda's diplomatic representative after the general made threats against foreign mercenaries operating in eastern DR Congo.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The 52-year-old general, widely seen as a potential successor to his father Yoweri Museveni, has become known for his provocative social media posts.
sentences.article_title: DR Congo demands answers over Ugandan general's threats

sentences.text: The flooded mine is in Bogor in West Java It's been three days since Rani last saw her father as he left for work on Monday.

sentences.text: Early on Tuesday, she received news that he was trapped underground.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: Above ground, ambulances and medical personnel are ready and waiting to transport victims.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: "We are coordinating with all search and rescue personnel involved in the operation to monitor water conditions and assess access to the mine shaft," Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, said in a statement on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: Multiple studies show that over the past ten years the illegal industry has rapidly flourished, often in correlation with rising gold prices.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: In early 2026, those prices reached an all-time high – spurring a gold rush that prompted mine operators across the country to expand their operations.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: But Bisman Bakhtiar, Executive Director of the Center for Energy and Mining Law Studies, told the BBC earlier this year that the actual number of illegal mines in Indonesia is higher than the government's figures.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: "[The government figures are] what's been recorded.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: That means there must be more than that," he said, noting that law enforcement operations have had little impact on the sector.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: Laode M Syarif, former deputy chairman of the Corruption Eradication Committee, said that unofficial mining is difficult to eradicate because every illegal mine has "backing", usually from "police and military or high-ranking officials in local and provincial governments".
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: "As long as these backers are not dealt with firmly, illegal mining will continue," he said.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: In many cases, though, the allure of these mines is simple: they offer an economic lifeline to people with few other viable prospects.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: But the lack of regulation and poor construction in the pits also means accidents are relatively common – whether from landslides, floods, or exposure to hazardous gases, all of which have claimed lives in recent years.

sentences.text: Relatives of the missing Bogor miners have been waiting near the site for news of their loved ones Earlier this year, in the same area as this week's flooded mine, 11 illegal gold miners reportedly died after a carbon monoxide leak inside a shaft.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: Elsewhere, in West Sumatra, nine people were killed at an illegal gold mine in May after heavy rain triggered the collapse of a 30-metre cliff, burying 12 miners in total.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: There are numerous reports of other such incidents across the Indonesian archipelago.
sentences.article_title: Thirteen dead as mine disaster highlights illegal hunt for gold

sentences.text: But the illegal nature of the small-scale gold mining sector obfuscates the true number of casualties.

sentences.text: "This should be a momentum for all parties to resolve the [illegal gold mining] problem comprehensively, not just taking action after the incident or closing the holes discovered," said Abdul Ghoffar, a member of the Indonesian Ombudsman.

sentences.text: Katherine's ex-partner was arrested 28 times for stalking her A new standalone offence of stalking is to be created in England and Wales after a review found the law regarding the crime was "cluttered and confused" - but the maximum sentence will not be increased.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Specific stalking offences were introduced in 2012 but the underlying offence of harassment had to be established, and additional factors such as fear or distress proven, for it to be considered stalking.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: A review was ordered by the government last year, led by Richard Wright KC, who prosecuted the man who stalked and murdered Alice Ruggles in Gateshead in 2016.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Victims of stalking have welcomed the change in law but said they were disappointed not all the recommendations have been adopted.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Katherine, from Newcastle, whose former partner was arrested 28 times for stalking her, welcomed the government's decision to introduce one stalking offence instead of two.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: "I'm pleased about that one because my ex was charged with [the lesser offence] of stalking without fear to start with and I was terrified," she said.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Ashley, from Washington, in Tyne and Wear, was also disappointed the maximum sentence would not be increased.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: "Stalking can have a devastating and lifelong impact on victims and their families," she said.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The government has accepted the introduction of a single offence for stalking that can be tried in either Crown or magistrates' court and described it as the "biggest shake-up of stalking laws in more than a decade".
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: But documents seen by the BBC show ministers rejected Wright's proposal to raise the maximum sentence from 10 to 14 years.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Ministers said the average sentence for the more serious stalking offence in the year to March was 18.6 months, suggesting the existing maximum was not being fully used.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur said: "It's really important that victims know that we are holding perpetrators to account and feeling the full force of the law.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: "The average sentences being given aren't good enough." She said judges were already able to jail stalkers for 10 years so it was better to work with them to make sure they used the powers available to them than "changing the goal posts" on the maximum sentence.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Satvir Kaur MP, safeguarding minister, says the changes are the biggest in a decade The review was submitted to ministers earlier this year and last month Alice Ruggles's father, Clive Ruggles, said victims of stalking would be at greater risk of dying if the government failed to publish and act on the recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Originally from Leicestershire, Alice was killed in her Gateshead flat by her ex-boyfriend Trimaan Dhillon, who was found guilty of murdering the 24-year-old and jailed for 22 years.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Her family has campaigned for better recognition of stalking and improvements in how it is tackled.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Reacting to Thursday's announcement, Alice's parents said they "welcomed" the report and recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: They added they were "heartened" that the response "endorses the need for a single stalking offence that focuses on the perpetrator's behaviour and removes the onus on police and the CPS to prove the impact upon the victim".
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Wright's review concluded confusion between stalking and harassment laws could contribute to failures in identifying and prosecuting the crime.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: A previous investigation into police handling of stalking found three in every 20 stalking crimes examined had been incorrectly recorded as other offences, including harassment.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The review also recommends removing the need for victims to demonstrate actual fear or serious disruption to their lives for a stalking offence to be established.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Wright argues this would better protect victims who were unaware they are being secretly followed or monitored.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The government said it would explore introducing such a test but had not yet committed to its inclusion in the new offence, although Kaur said she was "sick and tired of it being the onus on the victim".
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The review called for more consistent police investigations and greater use of specialist interventions to protect victims.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: It also raised concerns about stalkers using applications to change protective orders as a means of maintaining contact with, or control over, victims.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Wright suggests additional safeguards, including requiring court permission before certain applications can proceed and ensuring victims can make representations.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The government acknowledged the problem but said it needed to explore the suggestions further.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Ashley, who was stalked by her former husband Jason Howe using an AirTag to track her movements, said she was "genuinely disappointed" by this response.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Howe was jailed for three years and four months in March last year for stalking and controlling or coercive behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: But Ashley later discovered a restraining order designed to protect her had been amended, without her being consulted, allowing him to use a road through an exclusion zone near her home.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: "A restraining order is supposed to protect victims, not provide another opportunity for perpetrators to maintain control," she said.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The government has decided not to adopt a recommendation that would allow previously convicted stalkers to face a new stalking prosecution after just one further incident involving the same victim.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: Instead, in previously announced legislation which comes into force on Thursday, courts will now be able to use stalking protection orders in cases of both conviction or acquittal.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: "These orders can be in place for as long as is needed," Kaur said.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The government said it would introduce the new legislation as soon as parliamentary time allowed, but had not set a date.
sentences.article_title: Stalking law simplified to become one offence

sentences.text: The experts say they are "perplexed" by Andy Burnham's stance on Welsh devolution Four of Wales' leading constitutional experts say they want to see the evidence behind Prime Minister Andy Burnham's rejection of calls for more powers to be transferred to Wales.

sentences.text: Millions of drivers who were mis-sold car finance agreements could face further  delays to compensation after the financial regulator said it had made some errors in its calculations.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Driver have already been told they must wait until at least 2027 to receive compensation, although some may be offered an early settlement.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Average payments of about £829 are expected under the rules published by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA).
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: However, legal challenges to the scheme - which will be heard in February 2027 -mean compensation calculations and payments have been delayed.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The vast majority of new cars, and many second-hand ones, are bought with finance agreements.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Customers pay an initial deposit to secure the vehicle, then a monthly fee with interest.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Compensation could be given to many of those who took out a car loan between April 2007 and November 2024.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The decision by the FCA, the financial regulator, applies to about 12 million car loans - about 37% of the total number during the period.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: In 2021, the FCA banned deals where car dealers received commission from lenders, based on the interest rate charged to the customer.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: These were known as discretionary commission arrangements (DCAs) and customers were often not told about them.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The FCA said this provided an incentive for a buyer to be charged a higher-than-necessary interest rate, leaving them paying too much.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Other car buyers were also judged to have signed unfair contracts because the commission paid to the dealer was so high - accounting for 39% of the total cost of credit and 10% of the loan.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Some customers were not given accurate information about the best finance deal because of exclusive arrangements between car dealers and lenders.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Under the latest proposals, the FCA expects average payouts of £829 per mis-sold agreement.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The total cost of the compensation, including administrative costs, could hit £9.1bn.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: How much individual consumers receive will depend on the degree of harm suffered.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The FCA has announced some claimants might be offered an early settlement, but only if it as good as what would be paid under the current proposed central scheme.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Complaints have already been made about four million finance agreements.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Those people do not need to do anything.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The regulator urged anyone who has not yet complained to contact their car loan provider directly, rather than using a third-party claims management company.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The regulator's central compensation scheme allows people to complain and potentially receive compensation for mis-sold deals without the need for a lawyer or to go through the courts.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Motorists have also been warned to be on the alert for scammers posing as car finance lenders offering fake compensation .
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: FCA boss Nikhil Rathi told the BBC's Today programme there are "many law firms out there who would like to get 30% of any compensation", stressing that the regulator's scheme  was "free to use" for consumers.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Millions of drivers were in line to receive compensation this year, and most of the remainder should have got compensation by the end of 2027.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: But the FCA has confirmed that no compensation will be paid before 2027 as a result of legal challenges to the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The watchdog has now said it uncovered some mistakes in how it categorised a small group of loan agreements under its redress scheme, which could have a small impact on compensation levels.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: "While the potential impact on average compensation is small – less than £10 per agreement, on average – we recognise this affects the ongoing litigation," the FCA said.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: That could leave average payouts somewhere between £819 and £839.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: "We will discuss with the challengers and the court the impact on this deadline, and for the timeline of the litigation." Consumer Voice has said the scheme leaves "too many people short-changed" .
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The FCA has also received challenges from three lenders: Volkswagen Financial Services, Mercedes Benz Financial Services, and Credit Agricole Auto Finance.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The UK's Upper Tribunal has agreed to hear legal challenges to the scheme, with a hearing scheduled for 16 February to 3 March.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: It means that lenders will no longer need to calculate or pay compensation to people owed money under its scheme, until the legal process concludes.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The FCA said it would need to decide what to do next if the courts decided to overturn the programme.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Without a scheme in place, the FCA has estimated that up to 19 million complaints would need to be handled individually, taking three years and costing lenders £6bn more.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: It said it would "defend the scheme robustly as lawful and the best way to resolve such a widespread, long running and complex issue".
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Ultimately, the industry is expected to cover the full costs of any compensation scheme, including any administrative costs.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Lenders - including some of the UK's biggest banks and specialist motor finance firms - have already set aside billions of pounds for potential payouts.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The FCA said a minority of claimants will be made early offers, but most will have to wait for the outcome of next year's court case.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: With huge compensation payouts inevitable, Barclays will offer early settlements to some claimants, with others expected to follow suit.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: However, the FCA said it had asked Barclays to pause making compensation offers while it worked the errors it identified in November.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The FCA has published a factsheet to help drivers , external work out whether they should accept early settlements from lenders.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Accepting would mean quicker payouts but remove them from any changes to the central scheme.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The body that represents the lending industry, the Finance and Leasing Association, said it had "concerns" about the central programme but that it was choosing not to raise a legal challenge.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Santander, Barclays and Lloyds also accepted the scheme, despite raising concerns that the level of redress is disproportionate to those who suffered harm.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: Even if drivers are entitled to compensation from these lenders they will need to wait.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: There were some concessions made to lenders in a scaled-down final compensation plan from the FCA.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The Supreme Court considered three test cases which influenced the FCA's decision and, ultimately, limited how broad the compensation programme could have been.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: It focused on whether the car dealers had a duty to act on behalf of their customers, rather than in their own interests.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: The test case which was upheld was that of Marcus Johnson , who bought his first car - a Suzuki Swift - in 2017.
sentences.article_title: Car finance compensation payments explained

sentences.text: In his case, the Supreme Court said the terms of his finance deal were unfair due of the size of the commission payment, and the fact he appeared to have been misled over the relationship between the finance firm and the dealer.

sentences.text: DJ Ralph Lawson rediscovered a tape that Daft Punk gifted him in 1997 Daft Punk have become household names after storming the charts with One More Time and Get Lucky - with an intimate set in 1990s Leeds lingering in the memories of attendees.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Now, those recollections have been reignited by the discovery of a lost mix by the French electronic duo hidden for several decades.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It all started when I opened a show for Daft Punk in 1997," says Ralph Lawson, standing on the top floor of the Mint XL club in the city centre.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: The 2,500-capacity venue is empty aside from staff testing out a staggering number of lights, bouncing off the spotless floors.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: It is a far cry from Ralph's first clubs when he started DJing back in 1991.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: He is a co-founding resident DJ at the legendary Back to Basics club - a DIY house music event that became one of Europe's longest-running club nights, hosting global stars until sunrise.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Mint evolved from an intimate Leeds club into festivals, large-scale productions and the new Mint XL club Ralph is holding up a digital audio tape (DAT) - a discontinued method of recording high quality audio.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: On its side are the handwritten words: "Daft Punk Mix Feb '97." "Daft Punk got so big so quickly, they were on such big stages at festivals that they did not really DJ," remembers the music producer.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "That is what makes the tape rare." The French pair were rapidly rising to fame when they were booked for Back to Basics, but they were pipped to the headline slot by drum and bass pioneer Goldie.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Daft Punk were on their rapid rise to stardom when they visited Leeds in 1997, but did not top the bill By the time the night arrived, Ralph recalls "there were queues around the block".
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Despite accidentally jogging one of their records during the set, Ralph got on well with both Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo - even if the latter only uttered a few words to him.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I would not say I was best mates with them, but I could get on a guest list," says Ralph.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Whatever their relationship, it was strong enough that Daft Punk sent Ralph a gift in the post - an hour-long mixtape for his radio show on Kiss 105 FM.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: This is the only picture Ralph has of Daft Punk playing their DJ set in Leeds After it was played out on air, Ralph forgot about its existence for decades.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: He finally rediscovered it during a root around in some old storage boxes, but there was a problem.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It immediately ripped," he says.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I took it out and there were two bits of tape hanging out." Despite being in a dry studio, mould had found its way in.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: When Ralph tried to play the tape it immediately ripped Spurred on by his social media followers begging for him to salvage the mix, Ralph found a company that preserves tapes in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "The problem with DAT is that it is incredibly fragile," says Adrian Finn, from  Greatbear, one of the people tasked with fixing the broken tape.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: He estimates the team spent hours across multiple weeks on this "difficult job", carefully disassembling the tape, repairing the rips and getting rid of the mould.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It's nice to make people happy through this kind of restoration work," says Adrian, who admits he was dancing around "a little bit" while listening back to the mix.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I thought it was good and glad it played back with hardly any errors." Adrian Finn from Greatbear in Bristol was one of the people tasked with fixing the mixtape Back at Mint XL in Leeds, Ralph cannot help but grin as he recounts attempting to play the mix for a second time.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "I was literally floored," he laughs, toppling over in delight once the kick drum blasted out of his speakers.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Ralph had no idea what the first track of the hour-long mix would be, so when it was one of his favourites - Everybody Dancing by the late American DJ Romanthony - he knew it would be "very special".
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: Ralph dropped to the floor in celebration when he heard the tape for the first time It is the "rawness" of the vinyl mix - complete with crackles and impressive manual transitions - that Ralph adores.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "It's a testament to the times," he says.
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: "Not as polished as things are now, where people can see precisely how in time they are and have visual cues." While the discovery may be a success for the nostalgia and memories of 1990s clubbing, Ralph also hopes the tape and the meaning behind it will inspire the next generation of DJs, music curators and artists.

sentences.text: "I want them to think, 'I could get behind the decks or find the next Daft Punk and put them on at our night', and there's the space for them to do that in Leeds." Will another French electronic music duo stop by in Leeds on their way to global stardom?
sentences.article_title: DJ gets lucky after finding lost Daft Punk mixtape

sentences.text: The Fender Stratocaster is widely considered to be the best-known shape in electric guitars Hans Thomann leads the way through his music store in central Germany to the large electric guitar department, where the walls are hung with hundreds of instruments.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Brands on show include famous names Fender and Gibson, plus Harley Benton.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The latter is a low-price range of guitars owned by the family-run company that Thomann leads – Thomann, one of the world's largest online retailers of musical instruments.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The shop, together with warehouses and offices, are at the company's headquarters in the tiny village of Treppendorf in rural Upper Franconia, in Bavaria.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The business was founded by Thomann's father, Hans Thomann Senior, in 1954.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: In one corner of the store, a young man is trying out a Fender Stratocaster, one of the world's most iconic electric guitars.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Designed in the US in the early 1950's, the "Strat" became the instrument of choice for many famous rock and pop musicians, such as Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton and Buddy Holly.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Hendrix famously set one on fire at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967, and his performances helped make the guitar a symbol of modern rock music.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Hans Thomann says that Fender's letter came as a big surprise These days, the Stratocaster is very much on Hans Thomann's mind, because it's the subject of an intense copyright dispute.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: When the guitar was first made, California-based Fender did not trademark the body shape.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: So, since the 1960s Strat-shaped guitars have been made and sold around the world by countless manufacturers.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The shape is so ubiquitous that many musicians consider it to be a generic design.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: But since March of this year, Fender has begun a new campaign to defend its right to the guitar's sinuous shape.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: It follows a decision by a court in Düsseldorf last December which granted Fender copyright protection , external of the Stratocaster design in Germany.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The defendant, Chinese seller Yiwu Philharmonic Musical Instruments, did not appear.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The Düsseldorf court accepted Fender's arguments and ruled in its favour.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: According to German law the court makes its decision based on the facts presented by the plaintiff if the defendant doesn't raise objections.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The ruling said that Fender's design for the Stratocaster was "an outstanding, free creative achievement" that "clearly reflects the personality of its author".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: It described the guitar as "a body without edges" with "soft curves that evoke associations with the female torso consisting of hips, waist and arms".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: On its website, Fender announced in March , external the decision created "enforceable rights" against any guitars using the Strat body shape, that are manufactured, sold or distributed into Germany or other EU countries, "regardless of where those guitars are produced".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Fender began to send out cease and desist letters to dozens of retailers and manufacturers, both large and small, asking them to stop making and selling Strat lookalikes heading for Europe.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: One of these letters, seen by the BBC, said Fender "insists that you immediately stop manufacturing, marketing, selling and producing the infringing products".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The letter also demanded that companies recall and destroy the guitars.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Jimi Hendrix helped to make the Fender Stratocaster famous The move caused an outcry in the guitar world, among manufacturers and musicians.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "Time to boycott Fender," one person wrote on the Facebook page of the boutique US guitar maker, LSL Instruments.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Thomann received a cease-and-desist letter shortly after a visit to Treppendorf in March by Fender's chief executive Bud Cole.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "We remember the meeting as a very positive and constructive exchange," says Thomann.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "At the time we had no indication that Fender was considering legal action." The letter, he says, came as a shock.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "For more than 70 years, we have carried Fender instruments with great appreciation for the brand and many of us are Fender players ourselves.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: We were therefore surprised and disappointed by Fender's recent actions." In 2025, Thomann sold over 112,000 Strat-style guitars, including more than 16,000 made by Fender and Fender subsidiary brand Squier.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "As a retailer, we want to continue offering our customers everything that is available in the world of guitars," adds Thomann.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Thomann says that the Düsseldorf ruling was simply a default judgement based on missed deadlines and didn't represent a "comprehensive review of the legal claims".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: For its part, Fender, which is majority-owned by Hawaii-based company Servco Pacific, says it has a responsibility to protect the Stratocaster's iconic design.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: In July, it sued Thomann in a German court, for copyright infringement.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: In a statement to the BBC, Fender said it remained "confident" in the original Düsseldorf court judgement.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "Our preference has always been to keep lines of communication open and resolve these matters through constructive dialogue rather than litigation," it added.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: With the legal cases continuing, Thomann says he believes it is important to get "legal clarity – not only for us but for the wider guitar industry." "Ultimately, we want to help preserve an environment in which innovation, diversity and creative development can continue to thrive," he adds.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: The Stratocaster is the most used emoji for a guitar Thomann says he was taking legal action not just for his company, but for smaller music companies too.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "We used to be a small music shop ourselves," he says.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "Many of the smaller manufacturers, guitar makers and dealers affected simply don't have the financial and legal resources to conduct a legal dispute like this." One such company is LSL Instruments, a family-owned boutique guitar maker in California.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: Its director of sales, Johny Miller, told me that when they first received Fender's letter they were "pretty terrified and blown away".
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "They were asking us to retrieve guitars from dealers out there and destroy them and send them proof.
sentences.article_title: Guitar wars - the transatlantic battle over the Stratocaster

sentences.text: "So when we heard Hans Thomann got the same letter and responded by suing them… so that everybody in the guitar community could understand exactly what's going on… we were so thankful and grateful," he says.

sentences.text: Sophie Hope's credit score was hit by identity fraud Getting approval for a mortgage, a car loan or even a mobile phone contract can rest on a credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Sophie Hope was on the sharp end of just such a decision.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I first checked my credit score, it was excellent.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But then my mortgage application was suddenly denied by the lender because of my credit report.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was a massive shock as I'd never had bad credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: When I looked into it, my score had gone to 'very poor'," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It turns out, the Brighton-based nail technician and content creator, had been the victim of identity fraud.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Someone had opened accounts in my name across various catalogue sites and ordered multiple items, including a PlayStation 4 and Nike socks," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Without me knowing, the debt was transferred to a secondary finance company.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It spent three to four years accumulating in the background.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was only when I went to apply for a mortgage that I discovered how severely it had dragged down my credit score," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores are "backward looking" says Funmi Olufunwa Hope's experience shows how crucial a credit score can be, but, as in her case, it does not tell the full story.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "As a nation, we are overly obsessed with credit scores," says Funmi Olufunwa, a consumer finance lawyer and founder of financial education business, Hoops Finance.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Three firms - Experian, Equifax and TransUnion - produce credit scores in the UK, and they all work from roughly the same data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "A credit score is backward looking.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It's looking at what has happened in the past, which doesn't necessarily predict the future," says Olufunwa.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "But when somebody's looking to lend you money, they're looking at what actually is affordable," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Traditional credit scoring systems also disadvantage "thin-file applicants" - young people and recent immigrants to the UK who won't have built up a credit history.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But with more financial data available than ever before - and a growing appetite for AI to make sense of it - could artificial intelligence help lenders work out who is safe to lend to?
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In the US lending decisions will often hinge on a credit score from a company called FICO, which uses data from the big three credit assessment firms.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But AI-powered lending firms, Upstart and Zest AI have both built businesses which offer lenders an extra option when it comes to assessing a client's credit worthiness.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Thanks to our machine-learning models that look at more than 2,500 variables, we believe we can make significantly more loans at low prices to borrowers from every demographic group," Upstart said in statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But like with many other applications of AI into everyday life, there are concerns.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Consumers need to understand what information is being used to make decisions about them, and they need to be able to challenge something when it is wrong," Tucker explains.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores have been a contentious topic for decades for this very reason, says Sandra Wachter, professor of Technology and Regulation at the University of Oxford.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We are not assessing if past decisions were right," Wachter argues, adding, AI does not know about existing social inequalities that impact decisions and could just "replicate what it has seen in the past".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: While companies like Upstart and Zest AI see technology as a tool for financial inclusion, Wachter believes that real transformation requires accountability, as well as automation.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: She stresses that firms must apply existing regulations and establish new guardrails to ensure that AI does not simply perpetuate the biases of the past.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Not putting any safeguards in place will fortify, foster, and enhance discrimination." Upstart says it is tackling that issue.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We've invested in creating objective, automated evaluations to identify bias, and we've incorporated those evaluations into our model training process so it evolves to become even more accurate and more fair over time," the company said in a statement.

sentences.text: Photonic chips use light instead of electrons to process data "Photonic chips are on the verge of a breakthrough," says Ton van Mol of the Dutch research institute TNO.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: If van Mol is right – and TNO, the European Union and the Dutch government are backing the idea with millions of euros - then the technology could be a gamechanger.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: The chips which run today's society, from your phone and TV, to the vast data centres meeting our insatiable desire for AI, are mostly electrical.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: They process data by shunting electrons around tiny circuits – a single microchip produced today can contain billions of transistors, and sizes are measured in nanometres (one nanometre is a billionth of a metre).
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Because they use light instead of electricity, photonic chips are faster, use less energy and generate less heat than traditional computer chips.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Van Mol hopes for an acceleration in photonics similar to the one seen in electrical chips since the 1970s.
sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: "With optical chips, you are now where electronic chips were maybe 40 [or] 50 years ago." sentences.article_title: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave

sentences.text: Which is why the European Union has committed €400m ($450m; £330m) to a project called PIX Europe , external , with the stated goal of making the continent "a global leader in emerging technology for Photonic Integrated Chips".

sentences.text: A jet engine will have hundreds of turbine blades Every time you fly, an extraordinary feat of endurance occurs inside the aircraft's engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Hidden from view inside the sleek outer nacelle are hundreds of little turbine blades that can shrug off enormous mechanical stresses and temperatures exceeding 1,500C.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It is a true engineering marvel.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And these hardy blades are not sculpted or cut from their material – they are grown.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the 1960s, engineers worked out how to take a molten metal alloy, cast it into the shape of a turbine blade, and then cool it very carefully from one end to the other over a matter of hours.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A single crystal or grain of metal alloy forms during this process of gradual, delicate solidification.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Like turning a cup of water into one big snowflake, of your own design, rather than a mini blizzard of many smaller snowflakes.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's about as complicated as manufacturing gets," says Ben Fifoot, manufacturing engineer at Rolls-Royce, which makes turbine blades in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "It's a real motivator to get out of bed in the morning." Only a handful of companies around the world can produce these single crystal turbine blades, and the process has been perfected end-to-end in just five countries, including the US and UK.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Engine-makers continually vie for access to the technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Rolls-Royce, GE and France's Safran are among the few firms that have perfected the process.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: In September, GE Aerospace announced , external it would acquire its turbine blade supplier for $11.75bn (£8.78bn).
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Neither company responded to BBC News' requests for comment but the move has been described as an effort to ensure supply of these critical components.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Separately, in March, Rolls-Royce said it would invest more than £19m in its Rotherham blade casting facility.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Turbine blade specialists continue to work on improving the capabilities of this little-known technology.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: All the while, China is desperate to prove that its engineers can produce turbine blades of the same quality as those in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Who will come out on top?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Demand for [turbine blades] is huge.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: So few companies have managed to do it, which does give it this kind of magical aura," says Bill Sweetman, an aviation industry writer and consultant.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: He suspects GE Aerospace's recent move is about securing reliability and predictability in the notoriously volatile aircraft manufacturing supply chain.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The casts play a crucial part in the cooling process But why is the single crystal casting process, which has been around for decades now, still so specialist?
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: To grow one of these blades, asserts Fifoot, is to "fight the laws of the universe".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: This is because each molten blade would naturally cool into a solid object consisting of many small grains of metal alloy, all jumbled together.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But you don't want a crumbly sugar cube, you want a perfect diamond.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Getting a single crystal to grow into the shape of the blade instead isn't just a matter of cooling the molten version down slowly, the process also uses a bizarre trick called a pigtail.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The pigtail is a small spiral at one end of the blade.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Fifoot says that, at the beginning of the cooling process, this spiral "chokes" the flow of solidifying crystals so that just one takes over.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A bit like a hairpin corner in an F1 race right before the finish line – one driver can take the lead here and go on to win.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Sometimes we need to play around with the number of turns or the angles on [the pigtail] to try and get more favourable grain," adds Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Once the blade is formed, this crucial but sacrificial spiral is cut off.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: France's Safran is among the few companies that can make single crystal blades Blades made by Rolls-Royce are used in aircraft engines including the Trent XWB-84, which powers the Airbus A350-900, and the Trent 1000 XE, for the Boeing 787.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The single crystal is essential to ensure each blade's performance.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Sometimes a blade doesn't cool quite as planned, for example two crystals form within it instead of just one, and the metal alloy must be reprocessed so that the manufacturer may re-use the material.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Special ceramic coatings also protect blades from extreme temperatures inside engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And another important feature is that blades are cast with tiny channels that allow a flow of cooler air to coat them in a kind of film while the aircraft engine is working.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "The drive at the moment [across the industry] is currently to make those cooling passages really intricate," says Paul Withey, at the University of Birmingham, who formerly worked for Rolls-Royce.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The more turbulent those little flows of cool air are, he explains, the more they will knock heat out of the surrounding, much hotter air.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And blade-makers also seek to reduce the mass of these components as much as possible.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "If we can take any weight out of it, you can run that engine more efficiently using less fuel – you can spin it faster and hotter," says Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A report in May , external quoted one engineer at the AECC Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials claiming that China now had a single crystal alloy "superior to or equivalent to the second-generation single-crystal superalloys widely used in Europe and the US".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It costs less to make, too, apparently.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But the West has a "huge advantage" over China given that the majority of commercial airliner production happens there, says Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Supply chains and the latest innovations are generally clustered in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Plus, Western manufacturers also have lengthy safety records under their belts.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: China must compete on practically every aspect of aircraft manufacturing , external – by no means just on turbine blades – in order to make serious in-roads.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "You can definitely see that happening but it's a long, uphill struggle," adds Sweetman.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Demand for aircraft is currently high, which is already straining various supply chains in the industry.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: That demand could grow higher still, suggests Withey.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: During the next few years, one of the two main aircraft manufacturers, Airbus and Boeing, could launch a new short-haul plane , external , he says.

sentences.text: Then, the other would have to follow suit in order to remain competitive.

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?

sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: There were two significant moments at today's summit in that regard.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: First, Burnham said that the government had got as far as it could go with incremental deals with the EU, at least this side of a general election.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: In other words, he has got as far as he believes is possible with the strategy he inherited from Sir Keir Starmer of getting closer to the EU within the confines of the post-Brexit architecture set out by Theresa May all those years ago, of Britain remaining outside the single market and the customs union.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That suggests that after two years of this, there will not be a third annual summit to unveil specific agreements designed to smooth post-Brexit issues affecting specific sectors.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Yet it does sound like there will be another summit next year - or, rather, an "informal brainstorming process" about potential options for future relations with the EU.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That sounds pretty nebulous, sure, but an event dedicated specifically to both sides discussing how to change the terms of Britain's arrangements with the EU is likely to become quite a big moment when it arrives.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Perhaps as importantly, von der Leyen made clear that the EU was embracing this event too.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: That said, it does diminish the chances of major movement from Burnham towards embracing a specific model for the EU relationship in the intervening period.
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: And what of the domestic politics of this?
sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.article_title: Henry Zeffman: Burnham's first taste of EU deal-making unlikely to be his last

sentences.text: Welsh Greens leader Anthony Slaughter says the decision to part from Zack Polanski's party is a "positive step" Members of the Green Party in Wales have backed plans to split from their colleagues in England and form their own independent party.

sentences.article_title: Welsh Greens back plan to separate from English party

sentences.article_title: Welsh Greens back plan to separate from English party

sentences.article_title: Welsh Greens back plan to separate from English party
