sentences.text: Claire Waxman said the state was failing in its duty to keep the public safe The victims' commissioner for England and Wales has said the state is failing to keep the public safe, as she urged Andy Burnham to put the justice system at the heart of his 10-year plan for government.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Claire Waxman told the BBC that she would press the prime minister to commit to reforms in the decade-long blueprint, which he is set to unveil next month.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: She warned that the early release of prisoners to ease overcrowding in jails, along with long waits in the courts, had eroded the trust of crime victims to come forward.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: It comes as the commissioner's latest annual survey of victims, to be published on Tuesday, found many had experienced long waits for justice.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Nearly half of respondents whose case went to a crown court had seen their trial postponed, with over a quarter reporting the trial had taken place more than a year after it was originally scheduled.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Almost half of the respondents to the survey also said they were dissatisfied with communication from the police.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast, Waxman said the results showed victims were being failed "at every point".
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: The commissioner, who said she was due to meet Burnham in the coming weeks, said she wanted him to put a "real commitment to reforming our criminal justice system" as part of his 10-year plan.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: "It's been under-invested and mismanaged for so many years.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: That's why we're in the state that we're in," she added.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: She warned: "It can't continue.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Waxman also criticised the government's handling of the scheme, saying that victims needed further reassurance that they would be kept safe when offenders are let out under the programme to ease overcrowding in jails.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Around 5,000 prisoners are scheduled to eventually be released under the latest version of the scheme , the need for which Labour has blamed on a lack of investment in prisons under the Conservatives.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Waxman said that letters sent over the summer to warn victims ahead of releases had been "very poor" and lacked detail on how offenders were going to be risk-assessed prior to being let out early.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: She said she was "still waiting to see" data about the impact of releases on the ground, adding it had been around a year since the last meeting of the National Criminal Justice Board, an oversight body for the justice system.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: As part of the latest survey, the commissioner is recommending that all crime victims should receive a victim identifier number to track their progress through  the criminal justice system.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: The survey report will argue this would improve coordination between different agencies, as well as allowing victims to monitor when they will access the various legal rights they have under the Victims' Code.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: It will also call for an "end-to-end" review of how victims navigate the system, similar to recent reviews that have focused on sentencing or the courts.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: Responding to the survey results, Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones said the government was doing "everything we can to fix the broken system we inherited".
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: She added that ministers had already taken steps to improve the court backlog, and would be publishing an update to the Victims' Code next year.
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: She said this would be easier for victims to understand, and would set "clear expectations for criminal justice agencies and help victims feel supported".
sentences.article_title: State failing to keep public safe, warns victims' commissioner

sentences.text: The UK and EU have agreed a youth experience scheme which will allow a limited number of 18 to 31-year-olds to work, study or travel in the European Union for up to three years.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: Every year, 100,000 Britons will be able to participate in the scheme, with a reciprocal arrangement for 100,000 EU citizens.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: A joint EU-UK statement says the scheme is due to launch no later than January 2030.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: The numbers for both those coming to and from the EU will be allocated among the member nations according to each country's population.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: UK participants will initially be able to apply to travel to one particular EU country but can later switch to a different one, staying in a total of three countries during their three-year stay.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: However, they must spend 12 months in one country before switching.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: Visas issued by the EU or the UK will initially be valid for two years, with an option to extend for one more year.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: Neither UK nor EU citizens will be able to access benefits while abroad or bring dependants such as children.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: Participants will need to pay an application fee and prove they have enough money to support themselves during their stay.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: There are currently no details on what application fees UK citizens will have to pay, but the EU currently charges €90 (£75) for short-term visas.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: Numbers vary between countries for longer-term stays.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: The UK charges £340 for its other youth mobility schemes, in addition to a £776 annual health surcharge.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: The UK government has not said how much money an EU or UK national needs to have access to in order to take part but for similar schemes the figure is £2,530.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: There are no details yet on how places on the scheme will be allocated if it is oversubscribed; however previous schemes have used either a first-come, first-served basis or a random ballot system.
sentences.article_title: What is the EU-UK youth experience scheme and when will it start?

sentences.text: A review of the main disability benefit has recommended an overhaul of the system to allow disabled people to "achieve better health, higher living standards and greater independence".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report proposes both short and long terms changes to the personal independence payment (Pip) for claimants in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The benefit is claimed by four million people and is available to people whether they are in work or unemployed.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Its aim is to help with the additional costs of being disabled.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Pip benefit system 'not fit for purpose' and 'dehumanising' assessments should change, review finds - follow live This is the first review of the benefit since it was introduced in 2013.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: More than 40,000 disabled people engaged with the process with more than 90% of them saying they'd had a negative experience while applying for Pip, describing it as stressful, dehumanising or psychologically damaging.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review concludes the Pip process is "not fit for purpose" and calls for a fundamental redesign.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review was chaired by Sir Stephen Timms, the disability minister, the experience of disabled people is clear throughout the review.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A fast-track process should be introduced for two types of claimants.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those with terminal illnesses should get the fastest route to an award to ensure their lives are as comfortable as possible.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Those who have severe conditions that are well-evidenced and unlikely to change over time, and whose impact on daily living is clear, should also receive the benefit without a full assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Any subsequent review should avoid unnecessary reassessments.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Other claimants will have to go through an updated initial assessment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This will examine how a person's condition affects their daily life – functions, barriers, and needs that are currently not being met.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: This assessment will determine entitlement to the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will also decide the level of cash award, which will remain the bedrock of the benefit.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Optional referrals to support services should also be offered but this will be voluntary and a refusal to engage with them should not affect the benefit level.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: A new set of questions should be developed to better understand the extra costs a person faces, but will not ask them to calculate costs or provide receipts.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The system should recognise fluctuating and cumulative needs and produce decisions that are consistent and be robust against misuse.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The 28-day hospitalisation rule – which sees Pip payments suspended if someone spends more than 28 days as an inpatient – should also be reviewed as claimants find it can cause unnecessary stress and can delay discharges from hospitals.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The inquiry was not set up to find savings in the system despite the fact that spending on Pip is forecast to cost more than £40bn by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In the year before the Covid pandemic, Pip cost £16.3bn when adjusted for inflation to today's prices.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report acknowledges that since the benefit was introduced, the number of people receiving disability benefits has increased across every age group for both men and women.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Most of the increase has happened between 2019 and 2024, with the sharpest increases among young people aged 16-19, people in their 30s and women, whose rates of benefit receipt have risen faster than men's.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The report says that a reformed Pip system that more accurately reflects peoples' needs will likely mean "a rebalancing process".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: While the review didn't set out to make savings, it couldn't increase the overall costs and with some people likely to gain, others will almost certainly lose some cash.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: The review is not explicit on who these people might be.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Separate research last month from a think tank, the Resolution Foundation, suggested that one in six Pip recipients didn't have any additional costs associated with their conditions.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: In an interview to coincide with the review, Timms said that "if people don't have extra costs, then this is not the benefit for them".
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Alan Milburn's report - which proposed widespread changes to help get young people who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) into work across the UK - recommended that Pip be removed from people under 25 as part of a package of measures to tackle youth unemployment.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Today's review does not make the same recommendation.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: It will be up to the government to decide how they marry the two reports.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: They have said they are committed to reforming the Pip assessment process, but what that means in practice probably won't be known until the New Year when they publish their considered response.
sentences.article_title: Key takeaways from the Timms review into Pip disability benefit

sentences.text: Pip benefit system 'not fit for purpose' and 'dehumanising' assessments should change, review finds

sentences.text: Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Once established, it was effective.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: They included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the summer of 2021, as Covid restrictions were relaxed, around 7% of all UK adults were told to self-isolate over a seven-day period, something dubbed by the press as the "pingdemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes Treasury estimates suggesting that may have reduced economic growth by as much as 0.3% that month.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More than 200 doctors have had their details sent in error to the Times newspaper The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on the regulator's register.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Some doctors have also raised concerns that their ethnicity was included in the data breach.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: All the medics involved have been the subject of a complaint involving either antisemitism or Islamophobia, dating from the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023 to September 2026.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it has a legal and statutory responsibility to investigate such claims.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Times is understood to have promised not to make any of the  details public, but has said it will not delete the information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesman for the doctor's trade union, the British Medical Association (BMA), condemned the release of personal information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The BMA is aware that a number of doctors have received communication from the GMC to say that it erroneously sent personal identifiable data about them to the Times newspaper when responding to a media request," it said.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC must take action to ensure such a breach never occurs again." The BMA said it would look at ways to support members affected and urged them to make contact via their website.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A doctors' campaign group, The Doctors' Association UK (DAUK), called for an independent investigation into the error.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "If a doctor sent identifiable patient information to a newspaper, they could expect to be referred to the GMC," said Dr Matt Kneale, DAUK co-chairman.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC should hold itself to the same standard of confidentiality it expects from doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Just over a quarter of complaints over Islamophobia - 26% - have led to disciplinary action.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: But other complaints were closed, having failed to reach the threshold for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC said it had contacted the doctors affected to explain what had happened, to apologise and provide information and support.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesperson added: "We recognise the concern this will cause to both those impacted personally and other registrants and we are very sorry this happened.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "Our priority continues to be supporting those affected and taking steps to reduce the impact of this incident." Clarification 20 November: This article was amended on 19 November to remove references to the information being 'leaked'.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information was mistakenly disclosed by the GMC in response to a media request.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Adverts for tests and services relating to low testosterone are allowed but must be rooted in evidence, the regulator said Five adverts by online healthcare provider Voy have been banned by the watchdog for making misleading claims linked to low testosterone in men.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said the adverts promoted Voy's at-home testosterone blood tests in three posters and two paid-for Facebook ads.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: It said they were misleading as they linked common symptoms such as irritability and fatigue to low testosterone.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Voy said it had withdrawn the adverts while the investigation was under way and would not run them again.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The NHS says that while testosterone levels in men fall as they age, this is "unlikely" to cause any problems in itself.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: It adds , external that while a testosterone deficiency in later life can sometimes be responsible for symptoms such as depression, loss of sex drive, erectile dysfunction, and other physical and emotional symptoms, they are often not linked.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Voy is a company that sells products such as testosterone, menopause and weight loss treatments.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Some of its testosterone test kit adverts drew a backlash online earlier this year when they appeared on the London Underground.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Some described them as "ragebait" for using phrases such as "It's not him, it's his hormones" and "Men get hormonal too".
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: At the time Voy said it was trying to destigmatise conversations about men's health.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Some of the adverts sparked discussion online after appearing at Tube stations The ASA's ruling, however, took issue with how some of the adverts "exaggerated the connection between several common symptoms, which can have many possible causes, and low testosterone".
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The ASA gave examples such as low sex drive, low energy, loss of motivation and changes in mood.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: "While some symptoms may be more closely associated with the condition, others were much less specific and shouldn't have been presented as strong indicators of low testosterone in isolation," the watchdog said.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: It added that one of the Facebook adverts also included the claim that "low testosterone sneaks up on 1 in 4 men over 30".
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The ASA said this was misleading and not supported by the evidence provided by Voy.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: Dr Earim Chaudry, chief medical officer for Voy, said: "Every patient decision at Voy is clinician-led and these campaigns were developed to align with UK advertising standards.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: We keep all our advertising under continual review to ensure it meets any updated guidance." Wednesday's ruling followed two others in August by the watchdog, which found misleading claims in adverts for testosterone testing services from online providers BioID Health and Numan Digital Healthcare.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The rulings form part of a wider ASA investigation into adverts aimed at men concerned about their health.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: This has identified a "recurring theme of advertisers playing on insecurities around libido, erectile problems, testosterone and ageing", the regulator said.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: The watchdog said adverts for tests and services relating to low testosterone were allowed, but businesses needed to make sure the claims they made were accurate and supported by evidence.
sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.article_title: Cass report author tells BBC draft conversion practices bill is not workable

sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: NCVO chief influencing officer Leigh Brimicombe says it's quite clear charities are having to "subsidise" the NHS and wider public services and the government needs to address it by offering contracts that "cover the full cost of delivery".
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "Otherwise, we run the risk of services being reduced or cut completely, at a time that communities in need are relying on them most." For its part, the NHS is adamant that charities remain a valuable partner.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: NHS England points out that while the value of contracts to the voluntary sector in terms of proportion of the budget has dropped, it has still risen in cash terms.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: In a statement, NHS England told the BBC the current 10-year plan looks to build on the "potential" of these partnerships and given the sector a "stronger voice" in health and care.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: It's a complex relationship, believes Helen Gilburt, of the King's Fund think tank.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Charities bring "real benefits" through their expertise and close ties to communities, she says, and there is "an element of subsidising" as the NHS seeks savings.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But the situation has also "created inequalities" in the funding and support available for different diseases, she believes.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: For instance, some areas, like cancer, have an established charitable sector "which is able to attract large amounts of funding", she says.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: These charities have been able to advocate for their patients, work with the NHS to enhance specialist services, and use their funds to develop services of their own.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Then, she says, there are charities in some sectors - "Parkinson's and dementia are good examples" – which are investing their own funds to develop specialist roles.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "But they would argue this does not go far enough to meet the needs of people they serve.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "Then there are other areas, like sickle cell disease for example, where the charity sector is small and has even less funding." Democrats have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?

sentences.text: A bust-up between mathematicians is fuelling fears that AI could undermine science Inequalities exist within sectors, too, say experts.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Take hospices, for instance.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: "The fact remains that some communities will be able to give more than others, leading to inequalities in hospice provision," says Toby Porter, chief executive officer of Hospice UK.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: And as a result, says Sarah Scobie, deputy director of research at the Nuffield Trust think tank, "more people from deprived areas die in the place where most people say they don't want to die – in hospital".
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Not all of these differences can be explained by fundraising capacity.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Health literacy – people's ability to navigate services and advocate for themselves – can also affect access to support, she says.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: But her concern is clear – the scale of charity involvement in the NHS can widen inequalities.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: As Orton points out, the UK is not returning to the pre-NHS era, when healthcare depended on charitable giving.
sentences.article_title: The NHS is relying more on charities - and that might be creating problems for patients

sentences.text: Yet charities are no longer operating on the margins of the system, either.

sentences.text: Some public health experts argued that the proposed trial raised broader questions about whether vulnerable populations in African countries were being asked to take risks that researchers would not accept in wealthier countries.

sentences.text: Here is what you need to know.

sentences.text: The study was planned at the Bandim Health Project, a research centre that has operated in Guinea-Bissau since 1978.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: It was designed to involve 14,000 newborns, with half receiving a hepatitis B vaccine shortly after birth and the other half not being given the shot .
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Bandim said the trial aimed to investigate whether the hepatitis B vaccine given at birth has broader health effects beyond preventing infection.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Previous studies in The Gambia and Guinea-Bissau have raised questions about a possible link to increased mortality.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Researchers argued that because Guinea-Bissau does not currently offer routine hepatitis B vaccinations at birth, despite WHO recommendations, they have a unique opportunity to study its effects before such vaccines are introduced in 2028.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: But critics questioned the ethics of withholding the vaccine from some babies, particularly in one of the world's poorest countries, where the infection is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The Trump administration funded the proposed study, with the CDC awarding the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) $1.6m (£1.2m) in December 2025 .
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Walter Kazadi Mulombo, the WHO representative in Guinea-Bissau, told the BBC they became concerned after receiving questions about the study and finding no publicly available protocol.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He said the main ethical concern was that the trial would withhold an intervention already proven to protect newborns against hepatitis B.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The vaccine has been used for more than 30 years in more than 115 countries," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "A study that will withhold that intervention from other newborns is unethical." He warned that babies could be exposed to the virus during childbirth if their mothers were infected, as well as later in life.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Nearly a fifth of the population of Guinea-Bissau are infected with hepatitis B, a viral infection that affects the liver.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Those infected during infancy are particularly likely to develop chronic infections, which kill up to 25% of people, mostly through liver failure or liver cancer, according to data published in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The WHO is working with the government to bring forward the birth-dose vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The country had been expected to add it to its routine immunisation schedule in 2028, but officials are considering introducing it in the first quarter of next year," Mulombo said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Guinea-Bissau currently vaccinates children against hepatitis B at six weeks, which means it is less effective.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Guinea-Bissau's government prohibited hepatitis B vaccine trials involving children in January.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: At the time, it requested a team of experts from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to help evaluate the study.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Health Minister Quinhin Nantote said in October that the suspension remained in force and had not been overturned by the Council of Ministers after reports emerged claiming that the trial would be taking place after all.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "We were surprised to learn from media reports that the study might proceed," Nantote said.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "We are outraged because even I, as the minister responsible for this sector, was not informed." The dispute intensified after the SDU said a revised study protocol had received ethical approval "from the relevant authorities in Guinea-Bissau", which Nantote denied.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Dr Gavin Yamey, a professor of global health and public policy at Duke University in the US, criticised the proposal.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: "The proposed trial reeks of neocolonialism," he told the BBC, questioning why the research was not being conducted in Denmark.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: His criticism centred on the decision to withhold a recommended vaccine from some newborns in a country where hepatitis B is widespread.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: SDU dean Jakob Grauslund said the trial had never started, no babies had been enrolled and no vaccinations administered as part of the research.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The SDU said it had received a separate, positive assessment from the university's own research ethics committee.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Grauslund said the university had sought an additional independent assessment, although Danish law did not require one.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He added that the relevant Danish statutory research ethics bodies were unable to undertake the review.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Following the approval from the SDU's ethics committee, Grauslund decided that the project could proceed.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: He, however, stressed that this did not replace the separate authorisation required from Guinea-Bissau's authorities.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: On 19 October, Guinea-Bissau's Judicial Police searched the Bandim Health Project's facilities in the capital, Bissau, and seized a batch of hepatitis B vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Police said the batch was intended for vaccinating children but did not disclose how many doses had been seized or the specific grounds for the investigation.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: They stressed that the seizure did not, in itself, mean the vaccines were defective or unsafe.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The police have not explicitly said whether their investigation relates to the proposed trial, the importation of the vaccines or other circumstances surrounding the batch.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Grauslund said he could not comment on the seizure of the vaccines.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: The proposed trial was funded by the US government at a time of significant changes to vaccine policy under President Donald Trump and Health Secretary Kennedy.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Under Kennedy's leadership, a US vaccine panel attempted to end a longstanding recommendation that all newborns receive a hepatitis B vaccine at birth, but a federal judge later blocked this, along with other changes to vaccine policy made by the Trump administration.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Critics have questioned whether the research could help support that policy shift, although the study's stated aim was to investigate potential effects of the vaccine beyond preventing infection.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: Kennedy has praised the Danish researchers as "the deities of vaccine research", and cited earlier findings from their work in support of concerns about vaccine safety.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: A subsequent study by some of the same researchers, however, found no evidence of the previously reported effect.
sentences.article_title: Why a US-funded vaccine trial on babies was cancelled in Guinea-Bissau

sentences.text: There is no evidence that the proposed trial was designed to justify a change in US policy.

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.

sentences.text: Sweeping reforms are needed to help 440,000 more young people into work, according to former minister Alan Milburn.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Almost one million young people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - a current rate of 13%, which Milburn wants to fall to around 5% within a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: His government-commissioned review, due to be published in full on Tuesday, calls for ministers to intervene from early childhood through to adulthood, funded in part by radical changes to benefits for young adults.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Many of the review's proposed changes are specific to England, with some welfare and tax measures applying across all home nations.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, says extensive change is needed to avoid a "lost generation", and address what he describes as a "moral" crisis.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: By 2036, it says the aim should be for that ratio to be £2 on benefits for every £1 on work support.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "If we can get the benefits bill down, that is a good thing, but this is not about saving costs, it's about improving young people's lives," Milburn said.

sentences.text: The service would put a young person in touch with a named adviser to help to secure them an apprenticeship, college place, supported employment or a job within four months.

sentences.text: The review's key welfare measures, some of which have already been announced , suggest replacing these benefits for under-25s with a new Youth Allowance at the current base rate of Universal Credit for young people, and a new Additional Cost Allowance to replace Pip.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.

sentences.text: It is a question increasingly asked underneath social media videos, and often difficult to tell.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But there is a new trend when it comes to digital manipulation.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Across social media, AI-generated characters are appearing in videos that look remarkably similar to those posted by real people.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: From musicians to dancers and comedians, content creators are finding their performances cloned by these characters that are designed to look funny, realistic, or hypersexualised.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Experts call the practice "reskinning" and say it is made possible by cheap, easy-to-use AI tools.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: People can discover their work has been copied by seeing a video of a character making the same joke or doing the same dance, even with the same background.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Sometimes the AI version has millions more views than the original.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Some of the accounts identified by BBC Verify appear to be using these AI-generated videos to get views and likes, and to eventually make money.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Others appear to be experimenting with AI to make people laugh or simply for the attention that comes with going viral.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But the practice has angered content creators who say their original work is being stolen.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Lloyd says videos of her performances have been repeatedly reskinned by accounts that replaced her with over-sexualised AI-generated characters.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: One Facebook account published hundreds of short videos of a guitarist called "Mila Vasari" that had each gained thousands of views.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify found that at least three copied Lloyd's performances and used the exact same music, movements, and even facial expressions.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify did not find any evidence that "Mila Vasari" is a real person.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The videos on the Vasari account also contain visual inconsistencies that suggest AI was used to create them, including distorted fingers playing chords that don't match the music, and guitar strings that fail to move when strummed.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The account, which appears to be run from Canada, did not respond to questions about the purpose of these videos.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Its profile links to a page devoted to Vasari on Fanvue, a subscription platform that allows creators to charge for content, including adult material.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify has found two other accounts fronted by AI-generated guitarists that have reskinned Lloyd's performances and use those avatars to sell and promote adult content.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But Lloyd is far from alone in having her content manipulated by AI.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I've got so many messages from other artists and creators that have had the same thing happening to them," says Kjetil Krogstad, a Norwegian content creator known for videos showing him happily dancing in a suit while carrying a cup of tea.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: In March, his followers alerted him to the fact that one of his videos had been reskinned using an AI-generated bunny.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The post went on to attract millions of views - outperforming Krogstad's original video - before being deleted.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: When Krogstad looked into the account behind the bunny video, he found it promoting courses on how to make money from AI-generated content.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Dr Tina Kendall, an expert in online culture at Anglia Ruskin University, says that while these videos are sometimes made for fun, often the people behind the accounts copy videos that have already proven popular in the hope of attracting audiences and making money.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "What these tools allow people to do is just automatically take a viral concept that's already existing and to reuse it through these reskinning tools," she says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Kendall sees this as part of a wider online "hustle culture", in which accounts seek to turn users' attention and engagement into money - be it through subscriptions to fan pages featuring adult  content, risky cryptocurrency products like meme coins, or monetisation features on social media platforms.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: And making these copies "conventionally attractive, white, feminine" characters can help, Kendall says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I cannot explain how angry I am right now," Grace Roberts, a British car creator, said on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I put the videos side by side and I could see it was my exact facial movements, how my body moved, the exact same background and even the people around me were completely copied," she told BBC Verify.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "It was just me that had been altered." "I pay for the cars, I build the cars, I pay for the cameras, the filming equipment, and then someone can just hit download on their computer, change it, and then make money off the back of my video," she added.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters
